name: Filipino (Tagalog)

samples.note: "The fisherman bought the boat." Patient voice: the boat takes ang, and the fisherman is the agent (obj:agent).
"The fisherman bought a boat." Actor voice: now the fisherman takes ang. Compare with the sentence above.
"The teacher is reading the newspaper." Patient voice, imperfective aspect.

samples.text: Nagluluto na ng pagkain ang nanay.
samples.note: "Mother is cooking some food now." Actor voice, with the particle na.
"The child has a book." Mayroon expresses possession and existence.
"The table is in the kitchen." A predicate without a verb.

notes: Analyses come from calamanCy v0.2.0 (tl_calamancy_md), trained on UD_Tagalog-NewsCrawl, which is Manila news prose. They can be wrong. Validity is claimed only for standard written Filipino/Tagalog: not for Taglish or code-switching, social-media text, older literary Tagalog, or regional varieties.

Measured on raw text, punctuation included. Grammar-book sentences (UD_Tagalog-TRG, held out from training): UAS 93.6, LAS 76.8. News sentences (UD_Tagalog-NewsCrawl test): UAS 72.6, LAS 68.6. On news the published figure is LAS 77.1, excluding punctuation and with a different word alignment. On grammar-book sentences LAS is held down by a difference between treebanks: TRG labels ang as case, while this model learned det.
There are no phrase-structure trees for Filipino: no parser or treebank for them exists. SyntaxLab does not derive trees from dependencies.
The linker -ng is not split from its word (magandang stays one word), although the treebank analyzes it as maganda + -ng.

Known errors, shown as they are, not corrected: capitalized first words can get an unreliable lemma and aspect (Kumakain as Aspect=Perf), and adjectival predicates can be tagged as VERB (Maganda ang babae).

Sentence boundaries are found by punctuation, because this parser does not find them. Common titles and initials are recognized, but another abbreviation with a period can be mistaken for the end of a sentence.
The parser returns a single analysis even for ambiguous sentences.
